# 📊 opencode-quota **Spend windows of the connected providers — a ring in the session header and a panel tab.** [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@tuzelko/opencode-quota?style=flat-square&color=CB3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tuzelko/opencode-quota) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@tuzelko/opencode-quota?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tuzelko/opencode-quota) [![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/TuzelKO/opencode-quota?style=flat-square)](./LICENSE) [![OpenCode V2](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-V2-5B8DEF?style=flat-square)](https://opencode.ai) [![desktop UI](https://img.shields.io/badge/UI-desktop-8B5CF6?style=flat-square)](https://opencode.ai)
--- Every coding plan meters something: a 5-hour window, a week, a month. OpenCode shows the context ring, but not how much of the plan you already burned. **Quota** puts that next to the context indicator and opens the full picture in a side tab. ## ✨ Features - 💍 **Ring in the session header** — the used share of the smallest window of the current model's provider. Click it to open the panel. - 📱 **Narrow screens** — the same panel opens from the mobile view switcher under **More**, with the desktop layout and no separate UI. - 🗂️ **Panel tab, not a dialog** — every connected provider collapses into an accordion, with the current provider expanded; opening another closes the previous one. - 📈 **Every window, not just one** — percent, absolute usage and the reset countdown for 5 hours, week, month and top-up packs, whatever the provider reports. - 🟠 **Threshold colors** — orange at 70%, red at 90%, on the ring, the bars, the numbers and the composer pill. - ⏳ **Per-provider progress** — each provider's ring spins while its own request is in flight, so a slow provider is visible without blocking the others. - 💻 **Terminal UI** — a footer badge next to the context meter, a `/quota` panel with the same windows (run `/quota` again to close it), and a toast when a window crosses 70% or 90%. - 🌍 **Localized** — English, Russian, German, French, Chinese (the desktop UI; the terminal UI has no locale API and stays in English). - 🧹 **Only what you connected** — a provider without a connection never appears; one that is connected but silent keeps its last numbers and shows the reason. ## 🧩 Providers | Provider | Windows | | --- | --- | | OpenCode Go | shared 5-hour, weekly and monthly allowance | | Z.AI Coding Plan | 5-hour and weekly credits | | Zhipu AI Coding Plan (CN) | the same payload on the China platform | | Kimi For Coding (global) | 5-hour and monthly pools | | Kimi For Coding (CN) | the same on the China host | | StepFun Step Plan (global) | monthly Credit pool and top-up packs, or 5-hour and weekly windows on the older coding plans | | StepFun Step Plan (CN) | the same on the China host | The ring follows the model you run; the panel lists every connected provider. ## 📦 Install ```sh opencode plugin add @tuzelko/opencode-quota ``` Or straight from Git: ```sh opencode plugin add github:TuzelKO/opencode-quota ``` Requires OpenCode V2. The desktop app gets the ring and the side panel; the terminal UI gets the footer badge and `/quota` from the same plugin entry — the TUI loads the `./tui` part of the plugins its server already loads. ## 💻 Terminal UI The footer badge sits next to the context meter and follows the model you run: ```text Z.AI 43% 12.6K (1%) ctrl+p commands ``` | Action | How | | --- | --- | | Open the panel | `/quota` | | Close it | `/quota` again, or `/quota close` | | Force a refresh | `/quota refresh` | | Refresh or close from the palette | `ctrl+p` → "Refresh quota" / "Close quota" | The panel lists every connected provider, the current one first, with a bar per window, the absolute usage and the reset countdown. The header shows when the providers last answered and the `/quota close` hint. A window crossing 70% or 90% raises a toast. The terminal UI has no locale API, so its strings stay in English; the desktop UI is localized. ## ⚙️ How it works - **OpenCode Go** comes from the app's own usage store — the numbers behind the Console, one shared allowance across models. - **Z.AI, Kimi and StepFun** are queried by the server part with the key OpenCode already stores in the integration. Answers are cached for five minutes. - A provider with no connection is skipped entirely. A connected provider that fails keeps its last numbers and shows the error instead of disappearing. - The desktop GUI plugin API is experimental; the plugin uses only documented surfaces. ## 📝 Notes - Quota windows are a subscription metric. Pay-as-you-go providers report a balance instead, and are not shown; a Step Plan top-up pack is its own window. - The panel does not switch models; the model picker still does that. - The header pill is also available in a subagent session, where it reads the model from the session itself. ## 📄 License MIT © Eugene Frost
